issues.description: `pte_index` exports the less-than-512 `valid_pte_offset` guarantee while its decisive low-nine-bit range proof ends in `admit()`.
issues.rationale: All callers may rely on both the exact virtual-address offset and `valid_pte_offset(res)`, but the selected body delegates the masked result's `< 512` bound to a trusted assumption. The executable expression is mathematically correct, so this is a proof-boundary defect rather than a runtime-value bug. Repair 07236f8a preserves the exact result and range contracts and checks `(num & 511) < 512` with bit-vector reasoning.
issues.source_evidence: after/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/common.rs:82-98 computes the low-nine-bit index, promises `valid_pte_offset`, and closes the range assertion with `admit()` at line 96. Repair 07236f8a16d1bb38b73f0753ffff72c7fb07d7b7 keeps `returns va_level_to_offset(...)` and proves `(num & 511) < 512` by bit-vector assertion at repaired lines 92-96.
issues.verification: Compatible historical Verus reports problem vstd_extra 228/0 and lock-protocol 503/0 because the selected admit is trusted; direct repair reports 228/0 and 502/0. Fixed-source primary and independent reviews confirm that the repair preserves the result/range contract and replaces the trusted range step with checked bit-vector reasoning.
